title: Golden-Ratio Spiral — Exact Geometry, Statistical Inference and Dynamical Extensions
status: project mathematical theory derived from the recovered logarithmic spiral; empirical interpretations require separate calibration
abstract: The recovered Potato Axis spiral is one of the project's cleanest mathematical objects because its central properties follow exactly from a fixed logarithmic-spiral equation rather than from symbolic analogy. With r(theta)=a exp(b theta) and b=2 ln(phi)/pi, every quarter-turn multiplies radius by phi, reduces curvature by 1/phi and preserves a constant pitch angle. This redevelopment adds a full inference layer: coordinate noise, center/orientation uncertainty and competing geometry families are included in a likelihood so the fixed golden-ratio value of b can be tested rather than visually recognized. It also separates geometry from dynamics. A static logarithmic spiral is not a vortex; a vortex requires a velocity/phase field, circulation or angular dynamics. The theory therefore has two branches: exact geometric consequences, which are mathematically established, and dynamical spiral/vortex hypotheses, which require time-series data and additional equations. The scientific value lies in this separation: the same project equation can be tested rigorously without overclaiming a universal physical mechanism.

exact_geometry.meaning: These relations are consequences of the equation itself and require no physical interpretation.

statistical_fit.data: observed 2D/3D points transformed into polar coordinates relative to an estimated center/orientation
statistical_fit.measurement_model: ln r_i=ln a+b theta_i+epsilon_i, epsilon_i~N(0,sigma_i^2+sigma_int^2) as a simple comparator
statistical_fit.likelihood: ln L=-1/2 sum_i[(ln r_i-ln a-b theta_i)^2/s_i^2+ln(2 pi s_i^2)]
statistical_fit.golden_test: Compare H_phi:b=b_phi against H_free:b estimated from data.
statistical_fit.uncertainty: Center, phase origin, deprojection and measurement errors must be propagated; fixing them by eye can create an artificial logarithmic fit.

competing_models.generic_log: r=a exp(b theta) with free b
competing_models.selection: Use held-out prediction, information criteria or Bayes factors appropriate to the model and priors; do not compare residuals only after manually selecting favorable arcs.

scale_invariance.self_similarity: Rotation by Delta theta followed by scaling exp(-b Delta theta) maps the ideal spiral onto itself.
scale_invariance.invariant_statement: The curve is invariant as a set under T_phi up to the chosen parameter range/domain.
scale_invariance.research_value: This gives Axis/scale language an exact transformation law rather than a metaphorical use of scaling.

dynamical_extension.meaning: Once theta(t) is specified, the static geometry generates concrete velocity/acceleration relations.
dynamical_extension.counter_rotation: Two spirals counter-rotate only if theta_dot_1 theta_dot_2<0 over the relevant interval.

vortex_requirement.velocity_field: A fluid/field vortex requires v(x,t), not merely a spiral curve.
vortex_requirement.promotion_rule: Use the word vortex only when circulation/vorticity or equivalent phase-flow structure is defined and measured/simulated.

coupled_dual_spiral.observable: phase difference Delta=theta_2-theta_1 and radial ratio r_2/r_1
coupled_dual_spiral.question: Do coupling parameters improve prediction of observed phase/radius trajectories beyond independent spirals?

failure_conditions: A free-b logarithmic spiral substantially outperforms the fixed golden-ratio value where the golden parameter is claimed.
Archimedean/power/spline alternatives predict held-out data equally or better.
The inferred fit is unstable to plausible center/deprojection uncertainty.
A claimed vortex has no defined velocity, circulation or vorticity field.
Cross-domain occurrences of approximate spirals are treated as a shared physical mechanism without a derived coupling law.
next_decisive_work: Fit one real target using a center/orientation uncertainty model.
Compare fixed golden b against free logarithmic and non-logarithmic baselines.
If dynamics are claimed, recover/measure theta(t) and test r_dot=b r theta_dot.
Only then examine whether a common dynamic law survives across more than one domain.
